preconditions.description: The number of pairs n is between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.
The number of colors k is between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: stdout.startswith('NO') or (stdout.startswith('YES') and len(stdout.splitlines()) == n + 1 and all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: The output is either 'NO' or 'YES' followed by n lines, each containing two integers.

postconditions.expression: stdout.startswith('NO') or all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= k and 1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= k for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: If the output is 'YES', each color in the pairs is between 1 and k inclusive.

postconditions.expression: stdout.startswith('NO') or all(int(line.split()[0]) != int(line.split()[1]) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: If the output is 'YES', no pair has the same color for both the man and the woman.

postconditions.expression: stdout.startswith('NO') or all(int(stdout.splitlines()[i+1].split()[0]) != int(stdout.splitlines()[i].split()[0]) and int(stdout.splitlines()[i+1].split()[1]) != int(stdout.splitlines()[i].split()[1]) for i in range(1, n))
postconditions.description: If the output is 'YES', consecutive pairs have different colors for both the man and the woman.

postconditions.expression: stdout.startswith('NO') or len(set(tuple(line.split()) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])) == n
postconditions.description: If the output is 'YES', all pairs are unique.
